newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone to raise some fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone to raise some fuel prices.

text.p: Sierra Leone is to raise petrol prices at the request of the International Monetary Fund but has managed to persuade it to drop a demand that it also raise kerosene prices, senior officials said.

"The government yesterday officially informed the IMF in New York of its decision to increase petrol pump prices and the increase will take effect within the next few days," one official told Reuters on Saturday.
The increase will be in the order of 20 percent.
The government had earlier refused to comply citing the impact on the people of the impoverished West African nation.
The IMF, keen to cut Sierra Leone's budget deficit, linked an increase in fuel prices to continued funding. The IMF target date for the price increases was the end of March.
The budget deficit stands at more than $6 million.
The sources said that an IMF and World Bank team would visit Sierra Leone on March 27 to discuss future funding.
IMF officials in Sierra Leone were not immediately available for comment.
State radio, meanwhile, reported that President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah was leaving on Saturday for a three-day visit to Kuwait to strengthen ties between the two nations.

Sierra Leone is struggling to emerge from five years of civil war. Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule, signed a peace deal with rebels in November but implementation has dragged.
